I immediately wrapped my arms around Yuko, pulling her protectively against me. "Yuko, you don’t have to carry this. Let me handle them. These bastards thought they could touch Oka-san... touch you and Haruna... I’ll make them suffer ten times worse than anything they imagined."
One thug broke from his shock, face twisted in panic. "KILL THEM! KILL THESE FUCKERS NOW!"
They charged wildly.
I shielded Yuko as one brute tried to flank her with a raised bat. My hand shot out, seizing his throat. I lifted him effortlessly off the ground. His eyes widened in raw horror.
"W-what the—?! LET GO! AAAAAAAGHHH—!!"CRACK.
His neck snapped like dry timber. He let out a final gurgling scream, legs kicking wildly in the air for several long seconds before going limp. I hurled his corpse aside like garbage.
The others skidded to a halt, faces pale with terror.
I grabbed the blood-drenched knife from Yuko, my voice a low, venomous growl filled with pure rage.

"You worthless scum... You thought you could lay your filthy hands on my Oka-san? On my precious Yuko? On sweet Haruna?! I’m going to make every second of your remaining lives a living nightmare! You’ll beg for death before I’m done!"
I exploded into motion.
The first man tried to run. I caught him, swinging the knife in wide, deliberate arcs. I chopped his right arm off at the shoulder with a wetthwack.
"AAAAAIIIIIIIEEEEEE!!! MY ARM!! OH GOD, MY ARM!! IT BURNS—!! PLEASE!!" He screamed hysterically, blood jetting from the stump.
I didn’t stop. I hacked off his left arm, then both legs just above the knees, leaving ragged, brutal stumps. I avoided the femoral arteries on purpose so he would bleed slowly and suffer longer.
"GYYYYAAAAAHHH!!! NOOO!! STOP!! I BEG YOU—MERCY!! I’LL NEVER TOUCH THEM!! I SWEAR!! AAAAAAAGHHH—MY LEGS!! PLEASE, DEMON, KILL ME!!"

"You wanted to use these arms to grab Yuko and Haruna, didn’t you?!" I roared, voice shaking with fury. "You wanted these legs to chase down Oka-san while she screamed for help?! Feel it! Feel everything you planned for my family!!"
Another man swung his bat desperately. I caught it mid-air, tore it from his grip, and smashed both his kneecaps into powder.
"GGYAAAAAHHH—!! MY KNEES!! I CAN’T—!! PLEASE STOP!! I’M SORRY!! WE WERE WRONG!!" He collapsed, sobbing.
I stomped down repeatedly on his hands, crushing every finger into mangled pulp. "These hands that were going to violate my mother and sisters?! You’ll never use them again, you piece of shit!"
Two others had already pissed themselves in terror, dark stains running down their legs. "He’s a fucking demon!!" one wailed. "RUN!! RUN FOR YOUR LIVES!!"
They bolted.
I raised my hand. Telekinesis surged outward. Invisible force slammed around the five remaining men, lifting them helplessly into the air. Their limbs flailed uselessly against nothing.
"W-what is this?! I CAN’T MOVE!!" "LET ME DOWN!! PLEASE!! AAAAAHHH!!" "THIS IS IMPOSSIBLE!! HE’S A MONSTER!! A GHOST!! SORCERY!! NOOO—!!"
I floated one forward until his face was inches from mine. He was shaking violently, urine dripping from his dangling feet. "P-please... I have kids... let me go... I beg you, devil!!"

My smile was ice-cold. "You used these eyes to stare at my Yuko like she was meat. You imagined stripping Oka-san and Haruna. You laughed about making them scream. Now you’ll never look at another woman again."
I slowly plunged the knife into his left eye socket.
"GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHH!!! MY EYE!! IT HURTS!! STOP!! AAAAAGHHH—!!" His scream was ear-piercing, his body convulsing in mid-air.
I twisted the blade and scooped the eyeball out with a sickeningschlorp. Using telekinesis, I forced the bloody, twitching orb straight into his screaming mouth.

"MMMMMPHHH—!! GLURK—!! NOOO!!" He gagged and choked violently, vomiting blood around the eye as I clamped his jaw shut with my power, forcing him to swallow it. His muffled screams continued, tears and blood streaming down his face.
Several of the floating men passed out from sheer horror, bodies going slack.
I turned to the rest, my voice booming with righteous, enraged fury. "All of you disgusting animals thought about it!"

"Every single one of you fantasized about pinning down my Oka-san and breaking her! About making Yuko and Haruna cry and bleed while you took turns! For even daring to imagine harming my family, I sentence you to true hell!"
I layered Absolute Hypnosis over my telekinesis. Their bodies began marching against their will toward the corpses on the ground.
"Go home to your families," I commanded coldly. "Rape them. Kill them. Eat them. Make them suffer exactly like you planned to make my mother, Yuko, and Haruna suffer."
Their faces twisted in absolute despair. They still had full awareness.
"NO!! PLEASE!! NOT MY WIFE!! NOT MY CHILDREN!! I BEG YOU, DEMON!! HAVE MERCY!! AAAAAAHHH—!!" one screamed, tears pouring as his legs moved on their own.

"I’LL DO ANYTHING!! KILL ME INSTEAD!! DON’T MAKE ME DO THIS!! I’M SORRY!! SO SORRY!!" another howled, snot and vomit mixing on his chin. "MY FAMILY IS INNOCENT!! PLEASE!! I WAS WRONG!! FORGIVE ME!! GYYYAAAAHHH—!!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1104: Hypnotic Damnation: Go Rape Your Family
paragraphs: I pointed at the three bodies. "First, eat these three bastards completely. Flesh, guts, everything. Then you can go finish your own family."
Sobbing and screaming, their bodies obeyed. They fell upon the corpses, tearing into flesh with teeth and broken fingers while their minds remained fully conscious.
"NOOO!! I CAN’T!! THIS IS DISGUSTING—!! BLAAARGGHH!!" "MOM... FORGIVE ME... I’M EATING A PERSON!! AAAAAAAGHHH!!" "PLEASE STOP THIS!! I’LL DIE!! JUST KILL ME!!"
The wet sounds of ripping meat, crunching bones, and endless broken begging filled the night.

I turned away from the grotesque scene and walked to Yuko. She stood motionless, eyes wide with pure shock and disbelief, but not a single trace of fear. Her gaze shifted from the floating, screaming, forced cannibals back to me.

I pulled her into a tight, protective hug, gently stroking her hair. "Sister Yuko... are you alright? Did any of them hurt you? I’m sorry you had to witness this, but they deserved every scream, every second of agony for even thinking about touching you, Oka-san, or Haruna."

Yuko’s voice came out quiet, laced with stunned awe. "Jack... what... what are you? How did you do all of this? The floating... making them eat each other while they scream and beg... that power with the eyes... everything..."

I held her closer, shielding her from the horrific sounds behind us. "I’ll explain everything once we’re safe with Oka-san and Haruna. For now, know this: No one threatens my family and walks away. I made sure their final moments were filled with the same terror and helplessness they wanted to force on all three of you."

Yuko nodded slowly against my chest, still processing the supernatural brutality, her surprise clear in her wide eyes and slightly trembling hands gripping my shirt. Yet there was no fear—only deep trust mixed with astonishment.

"Let’s leave this place," I whispered, guiding her away from the campsite. Behind us, the men’s tortured screams and desperate begging continued without end as they devoured their former leader under my unbreakable command.
I kept my arm wrapped protectively around Yuko’s shoulders, guiding her through the darkness until the tent came into view again.
I reached the tent, unzipped the flap slowly, and stepped inside with Yuko right behind me. The warm lantern light revealed a scene heavy with emotion.

Kasumi—Oka-san—was sitting on her knees, eyes red and tears still streaming down her beautiful face. Her hands were clasped tightly together as if she had been praying the entire time. Beside her, Haruna sat with a bright, confident smile, completely unfazed.
The moment I entered, Haruna’s face lit up like the sun. She sprang forward and jumped straight into my arms, wrapping her legs around my waist and burying her face in my neck.
"Oka-san! Look! Didn’t I tell you Jack would be fine?" Haruna exclaimed happily, squeezing me tighter. "I knew he’d protect us! Jack is the strongest!"

Kasumi let out a deep, shaky sigh of relief. A soft, trembling smile broke through her tears as she rose to her feet and rushed closer. She reached out with both hands, gently touching my face, my shoulders, and my chest, checking for any wounds.

"Jack... you didn’t get hurt, right? Are you okay? Please tell me you’re not injured..." Her voice was thick with worry. Then her expression shifted as distant screams still faintly reached the tent. "What... what was all that screaming? It sounded so horrible... like someone was being tortured..."
She tried to move toward the tent entrance to look outside, her face filled with concern. Before she could reach the zipper, Yuko stepped in smoothly and pulled it shut with a firm tug.

"Mom, they’re all gone," Yuko said calmly, her voice steady despite everything she had just witnessed. "They were afraid of us. The moment they realized they weren’t a match, they ran like cowards into the forest. We won’t have to worry about them anymore."
Kasumi looked at Yuko in astonishment, blinking a few times before nodding slowly. I quietly extended my telekinesis, gently brushing against her mind to read her surface thoughts:
[Yeah... Yuko is an assassin after all. She can deal with anyone. I was afraid for nothing... Thank goodness they’re all safe.]

Kasumi turned back to her daughter, her maternal instincts kicking in fully. "Yuko, are you okay? Let me check you properly." She began running her hands over Yuko’s arms, shoulders, and torso, searching for any cuts, bruises, or blood.

Yuko suddenly smirked, a teasing glint appearing in her eyes despite the violence she had unleashed earlier. "Oka-san... now you remember your daughter? It looked like your son-in-law was much more important. You ran to Jack first, checking him so carefully. Am I less important now?"

Kasumi’s eyes widened in panic. "No! How can that be?! You all are equally important to me! I love you all the same—Jack, Yuko, Haruna... You’re my precious family. I was just so worried about everyone!"

Yuko wasn’t done. She crossed her arms, still riding the adrenaline, and glanced at her younger sister with a playful grin. "Oh? I didn’t see that, Haruna. Did you see it too? Looks like Jack has completely stolen our Oka-san away from us. She only has eyes for her strong son-in-law these days."
Haruna giggled loudly, still clinging to me like a koala. "Yeah! Oka-san was crying so much for Jack! She forgot about us for a second there!"

Kasumi’s cheeks flushed with a mix of embarrassment and slight panic. She waved her hands in front of her. "What nonsense are you two talking about?! What ’stolen’?! There’s nothing like that! I was worried about Jack because he was outside facing those dangerous men! That’s all!"

Yuko continued the teasing, her voice light but with a hint of lingering intensity from the bloodshed. "Mmm, I don’t know... You should have seen how fast you ran to hug Jack’s arm. Haruna and I might need to fight for your attention now that we have such a reliable man in the family."

I chuckled softly, still holding Haruna securely while reaching out to gently ruffle Yuko’s hair. "Alright, that’s enough teasing your mother. Oka-san was worried sick about all of us. I’m just glad everyone is safe and together."
Kasumi let out a flustered sigh, covering her face with both hands for a moment. "You children... always teaming up against me. Jack, please don’t encourage them."

chapters.title: Chapter 1105: A Mother’s Unconscious Slumber
paragraphs: I moved in a flash—faster than any human eye could follow. My hand gently but firmly pressed against the side of Kasumi’s neck, targeting a precise pressure point. Her eyes widened for a split second in surprise.
"Jack—?!"
Before she could react or speak further, her body went limp. I caught her smoothly as she collapsed forward, unconscious but breathing steadily.
Yuko and Haruna both froze in shock.
"Jack...! What are you doing to Oka-san?!" Yuko demanded, eyes wide.
Haruna’s voice trembled slightly. "Jack... Oka-san...?"

I held Kasumi’s unconscious form carefully in my arms. "It’s nothing dangerous. I just don’t want her to see what’s outside. She doesn’t need those images in her head. She’s been through enough worry tonight."

Yuko stared at me for a long moment, then sighed and nodded slowly, understanding the deeper reason. Her gaze shifted sharply toward Haruna, a clear intent forming in her eyes to knock her out as well.
Haruna noticed immediately and yelped, quickly ducking behind me for protection. "Don’t, Sister Yuko! Please don’t knock me out! I want to stay awake!"
Yuko looked at Haruna, then back at me, her expression serious. "Does she know about... it?"
I nodded. "Yes. Haruna knows everything about my abilities."
Yuko’s jaw tightened. A flash of jealousy crossed her face—raw, unguarded. Her hands clenched at her sides.
Haruna peeked from behind me and stuck her tongue out teasingly at her older sister. "That’s right~ I know everything about Jack. He’s my boyfriend, after all. Hmmph!"
Yuko’s eye twitched. "You little brat..."

I didn’t let the tension escalate. I lifted Kasumi effortlessly, carrying her in a princess style—her head resting against my chest, her body light in my powerful arms. We stepped out of the tent together.
Outside, the scene had transformed completely. The bloody clearing was almost pristine. The three corpses were gone—wiped clean as if they had never existed.
Only faint dark stains of blood remained soaked into the dirt, along with a few scattered pieces of torn clothing. The air still carried a faint metallic tang.

Yuko stopped dead in her tracks, staring at the spot where the men had been forced to devour each other. Her face paled slightly as the memory returned: their agonized screams, the wet ripping of flesh, the desperate begging.
"They won’t really... do all that... right?" she asked quietly, voice tight.

I looked at her calmly. "They will. This is the price they have to pay for their actions. For every disgusting thought they had about Oka-san, you, and Haruna. They’ll live out their own nightmare before the end."
Yuko shook her head slowly but said nothing more. We walked to the car in silence. I gently placed Kasumi in the back seat, making sure she was comfortable and covered with a blanket.

Yuko sat in the front passenger seat, while Haruna stayed in the back beside her mother. The engine roared to life, and we drove off into the dark forest road. The night was still deep, stars hidden behind thick clouds.
We had been driving for nearly twenty minutes when Yuko suddenly broke the silence.
"Stop the car."

I pulled over to the side of the empty road. The headlights cut through the darkness as I killed the engine. Yuko stepped out without a word. I followed her. Haruna remained inside, watching quietly through the window.
Yuko walked a few steps away, then turned to face me. Her eyes glistened with unshed tears, a mix of hurt, jealousy, and frustration clear on her face.
"Now tell me the truth, Jack," she said, voice cracking. "Even Haruna knows about your powers... but you kept it hidden from me? You don’t trust me?"
I stepped forward and pulled her into a tight hug. She resisted for a second before melting against my chest, tears finally spilling.
"It’s not that I don’t trust you, Yuko. I just... didn’t know how to tell you. I was afraid of how you’d react."

She stayed in my arms for a long time, the tension slowly melting. In the distance, the first hints of dawn were beginning to touch the horizon.

"...Thank you, Jack," she whispered softly, her voice barely audible.

I gently wiped the remaining tears from her cheeks with my thumb. We stood there for a few more seconds in comfortable silence before heading back to the car. The night air was cool and quiet now, the horrors of the campsite feeling distant.

We climbed back inside. I started the engine, and we continued driving down the long, empty forest road. The headlights sliced through the darkness as the first faint glow of dawn began painting the horizon.
After a few minutes of peaceful silence, Haruna’s mischievous voice suddenly piped up from the backseat.
"Sister Yuko... why were you hugging my boyfriend so tightly outside? Are you trying to steal him from me~?"

Yuko stiffened instantly in the passenger seat, completely caught off guard. She had clearly forgotten that Haruna was sitting right there in the back, watching everything through the window. Her face flushed a deep crimson, eyes widening in panic.
"N-No! It’s not like that! I... I wasn’t— We were just—!" Yuko stammered, completely flustered, her usual cool assassin demeanor shattering in an instant.
Haruna puffed out her cheeks dramatically, then burst into laughter. "Pffft—! Hahaha! Your face is so red, Sister!"
Yuko whipped her head around to glare at her little sister in the backseat, still blushing furiously. "You... You were watching?! And you’re not angry?"
Haruna wiped a tear of laughter from her eye, grinning widely. "What do you think? Of course I’m not angry, silly."

Yuko looked genuinely surprised. She bit her lip, hesitation clear on her face before she spoke again, her voice softer and more sincere. "Then... do you blame your sister? I’m sorry, Haruna... but I really love Jack too. I can’t help it anymore."
Haruna’s playful expression softened into something warmer and more mature. She leaned forward between the seats and gently placed her hand on Yuko’s shoulder.
"I know, Sister. You’re my big sister. We’ve always shared everything important. From now on... we’ll be together. All three of us. With Jack."
Yuko blinked, then slowly nodded, a small, relieved smile forming on her lips. She reached back and squeezed Haruna’s hand affectionately.

Kasumi accepted the bottle with a grateful nod, taking slow sips while looking between all of us. "Fainted...? I don’t remember feeling dizzy. Did those men come back? Is everyone alright?"

She disappeared down the hallway toward her bedroom.

Haruna immediately hopped onto my massive bed, bouncing slightly as she patted the spots on either side of her. "That’s right! Big sister and I are staying right here with you. No excuses."

"That..." Hitomi’s voice was barely a whisper.
"That means...?"
Akane didn’t answer.
She couldn’t.
The truth—that using Healing Touch shortened my lifespan—was too cruel to voice aloud.
Not here.
Not now.
Not when Tachibana and Hitomi were already breaking.
Yuko stepped forward, her voice firm despite her tears.
"Master... don’t be angry at Tachibana.
It was I who brought them here.
If there’s anyone to blame...
It’s me."
Akane whirled on her, her eyes blazing.
"Yuko..." Her voice trembled.
"Do you have any idea what you’ve done...?!" She grabbed Yuko’s shoulders, her grip painfully tight.
Yuko didn’t flinch.
She held Akane’s gaze, her own tears falling freely.
"I know..." Her voice was soft, but unyielding.
"But Hitomi... she was suffering...
And Jack... he chose to do this.
For her."
Hitomi, pale, stepped forward.
"Master... what’s going on...?
What happened...?"
Akane didn’t answer at first.
She just stared at me, her red eyes—visible even through my closed lids via AI Lens—filled with a grief so deep it felt like a physical weight.
Then, she whispered, her voice raw.
"It’s... nothing..." She swallowed hard.
"I’m just... worried.
Something... will happen to him..."
She paused, her fingers tightening around the edge of the bed.
"Jack said using his ability makes him weak... and then he becomes normal again...
But I’m afraid..." Her voice dropped to a whisper.
"I’m afraid it’s not that simple..."
She didn’t say the rest.
She couldn’t.
The truth—that every time I used Healing Touch, my lifespan dwindled—was too brutal to speak aloud.
Not when Tachibana was already shaking, not when Hitomi’s eyes were wide with horror.
Tachibana stammered, his voice desperate.
"M-master...
Jack said his ability wouldn’t affect him...?"
Akane let out a hollow laugh, her tears finally spilling over.
"And you believed him...?" She wiped her face, her hand coming away wet.
"Even if it did... do you think he’d tell the truth...?"
The room fell into a suffocating silence.
Tachibana and Hitomi stared at each other, their faces drained of color.
"That..." Hitomi’s voice was a whisper of dread.
"That means... he knew...?"
Akane didn’t answer.
She couldn’t.
The weight of the truth was too heavy, even for her.
And then—
She collapsed to her knees, her hands covering her face as sobs wracked her body.
"Jack... you idiot..." Her voice was muffled, broken.
"You idiot...
IDIOT...!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1117: Akane’s Suicide Oath
paragraphs: I activated Telepathy once more, this time focusing on Akane. Her thoughts slammed into my mind, raw and unfiltered.

[You big idiot... Once you wake up... I will kill you... I will kill you myself... You are really a bother... Ever since I met you... There is always trouble... Why do you keep bothering me...? Why...?]

A bitter chuckle escaped my lips. This Akane... she’s such a tsundere. On the outside, she was fuming, her words harsh, her glare sharp enough to cut. But beneath it all? She was terrified. Terrified for me.
Her thoughts twisted again, the anger giving way to something far more vulnerable.
[If anything happens to you... Didn’t you think about what will happen to Haruna...? How will I face Yuko... and her mother...?]
[Please wake... Please wake...]

The desperation in her silent plea was palpable. It was the kind of fear that clawed at your chest, the kind that made your hands shake and your voice fail. And yet, she wouldn’t say it aloud. Not in front of them. Not when she was still clinging to her pride.
I smiled weakly to myself. She’s worried... but she’ll never admit it.
Hitomi’s thoughts, on the other hand, were laced with confusion and suspicion.
[What happened to Master...? Why is she behaving like that...? She’s hiding something...]
[I guess it must be something related to Jack’s ability... Did Master know...? Is that why she’s worried...?]
She glanced at Akane, her expression unreadable, but her mind racing. She wasn’t just curious—she was piecing it together. And the realization was dawning on her.
Yuko’s thoughts were a storm of denial and fear.
[What happened to Jack...? Why is Master so serious...? I haven’t seen her like this... Is he really okay...? If anything really happens to him... then... I...]
She clenched her fists, her nails digging into her palms.
[No... Isn’t Jack so powerful...? What could possibly happen to him...?]
[I need to ask Master...]
Her gaze flicked to Akane, her jaw set. She wasn’t going to let this go. Not when the man she loved was lying motionless in front of her.
Tachibana, ever the perceptive one, sensed the tension thick in the air. He stepped closer to Akane, his voice low but firm.
"Master..." He hesitated, then pressed on. "Are you hiding something from us...?"
The room fell silent.
Akane’s shoulders tensed. She didn’t look at him, her eyes fixed on me, her fingers tightening around the edge of the bedsheet. For a moment, it seemed like she wouldn’t answer.
Then—
"Tachibana..." Her voice was dangerously calm, but her hands were shaking. "This isn’t the time."

Tachibana didn’t back down. His fists were clenched tightly at his sides, his entire body trembling with a mixture of fear and frustration. "Then when is the time, Master...? Jack collapsed. He spurted blood from his mouth. And you’re acting like... like the world is ending." His voice cracked painfully. "We deserve to know the truth. No more secrets!"

Akane’s breath hitched sharply. She slowly turned to him, her red eyes burning with a terrifying mixture of raw anger and overwhelming grief. For a long moment, she just stared at him, as if debating whether to speak.

"And what if I tell you...?" Her voice was a broken whisper, yet it carried the weight of a scream. "What if I tell you that every single time he uses that damn ability... it eats away at his life...? That he’s dying a little more with every healing...? That he is literally sacrificing pieces of his lifespan for us?!"
The words landed like a death sentence in the silent room.
Tachibana’s face went deathly pale. He staggered back a step. "W-what...?"

Hitomi let out a heart-wrenching cry and dropped to her knees, her newly healed hands covering her mouth in horror. "No... Master... this is not true... Please tell me this is not true...! He healed me... he gave me my face back... and now you’re saying he’s... he’s dying because of it?! I don’t want this! I would rather stay burned forever than let him suffer!!"

Tachibana fell to his knees beside her, his voice shaking uncontrollably. "How can this be...? Master... why didn’t you tell me before...? I would prefer to die... I would rather stay dead than trade someone else’s life like this...! Master, why...? And it was me... it was me who brought him here... This is all my fault...!"
Akane took a deep, shuddering breath. She wiped her tears roughly with the back of her hand, trying to regain some composure, but her voice still cracked as she spoke.

"It’s because this idiot made me promise... He forced me to swear I would never tell any of you the truth." She looked at Tachibana and Hitomi with pained eyes. "That’s exactly why I was desperately stopping all of you from coming to meet him. I knew... the moment he saw Hitomi’s condition, he would use his power without hesitation."
Akane’s shoulders slumped as she continued, her voice growing quieter, "Now... we can only pray... that he didn’t use too much of his lifespan this time. Otherwise..."
She stopped mid-sentence, unable to finish the dark thought. The implication hung heavily in the air like a guillotine.

Akane then turned toward Yuko, her expression filled with guilt and self-loathing. "Yuko... I am so sorry. This is all my fault. If anything happens to Jack... I will commit suicide to atone for my sins. Actually... it was me. I was the one who went to your house that day to ask you to heal Tachibana. If you want to blame someone... blame me. Hate me. Curse me. I deserve it."

Yuko had fresh tears streaming down her face. She shook her head violently, her voice choked with emotion. "No... Master... I don’t blame you... It’s not your fault." She looked down at my unconscious form, her hands gently holding mine.
"It’s this big idiot... who keeps throwing his life away for us. If anything happens to him... what about Haruna...? What about me...? What are we supposed to do without him...?"
The room descended into a painful, suffocating silence. Only the sound of quiet sobbing could be heard.

Hitomi crawled closer to me on her knees, gently touching my hand with her restored fingers. "Jack... you fool... I was finally happy again... and now I feel like the worst person alive. All this beauty... at the cost of your life...? I don’t deserve it..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1118: Masked Tears of an Assassin
paragraphs: Tachibana bowed her head deeply, tears dripping onto the floor. "Master... I’m sorry. I should have listened to you. I never wanted to cause Jack harm..."
Akane remained on her knees beside me, gently stroking my hair with trembling fingers. Through the telepathic link, her inner thoughts continued flooding into my mind without pause:
[You stupid, kind-hearted bastard... If you leave me now, I really will kill myself... Don’t you dare die on me...]
Yuko leaned down and pressed her forehead against my chest, whispering softly, "Jack... please wake up soon. I still need to scold you... and then... I want to stay by your side forever."

I continued pretending to be unconscious for a long, agonizing time. Three and a half hours dragged by in heavy, suffocating silence. The tension in the room thickened like storm clouds, pressing down on everyone present.
Every shallow breath I took was carefully measured to seem natural, every slight twitch of my body controlled.
Tachibana paced anxiously back and forth across the wooden floor, her footsteps echoing sharply. She muttered under her breath, running a hand through her disheveled hair.
"This is too long... Why isn’t he waking up yet? It’s never taken this much time before. Master, please... say something, anything. We can’t lose you like this."
Hitomi sat rigidly beside the bed, clutching her now-healed hands tightly to her chest as if afraid they might shatter again.

Fresh tears rolled silently down her pale cheeks, leaving glistening trails. "This is all because of me... If I had just stayed hidden like I was supposed to... None of this would have happened. I’m so sorry, Jack..."
Yuko refused to let go of my hand even for a second, her grip tight and almost painful, her knuckles white. She whispered desperate prayers under her breath, her voice hoarse from crying.
"Jack... please... I can’t lose you... Not after everything we’ve been through. God, if you’re listening, bring him back to us..."
Finally, I decided it was time. I let out a weak, realistic cough that rattled in my chest, then stirred slowly on the bed, my eyelids fluttering open as if waking from a deep coma.
"Jack...!" "Jack!!" "He’s awake! Thank goodness!"
Everyone rushed toward me at once, their faces lighting up with overwhelming relief and pure joy, eyes wide and brimming with emotion.
But instead of the expected hugs and gentle words, Yuko’s palm flew across my face with a loud, stingingSLAP! The sharp sound cracked through the room like a whip.
I blinked, rubbing my stinging cheek with a weak smile. Yuko’s eyes were swollen and red from hours of crying, her lips quivering with a violent storm of relief, anger, and fear all mixed together.

"You big bastard...!" she shouted, her voice cracking painfully. "Are you trying to kill yourself?! Do you have any idea how terrified we all were?! We thought you were going to die right in front of us! We sat here for hours thinking this was the end!"

I coughed again softly, trying to play it off with a tired grin. "What are you guys talking about? I’m just a little weak after using the ability... It always happens like this. I’ll recover after some rest, I promise."

Tachibana stepped forward, her face twisted with a mix of anger, pain, and betrayal. "Are you really going to lie to us until the very end?! Master already told us everything! We know the truth about your lifespan! About how every time you heal someone, you’re carving away pieces of your own life!"
I pretended to be shocked, widening my eyes dramatically as I slowly turned my head toward Akane. "You told them?"
Akane remained deathly silent, staring at me with those complicated, pained crimson eyes that held a universe of unspoken suffering.

I looked at Hitomi and gave her a gentle, warm smile despite the exhaustion weighing on me. "Sister Hitomi... you look so beautiful now. The healing worked perfectly. Your hands... they’re completely restored. I’m really glad."

Hitomi burst into fresh tears, covering her mouth as heavy sobs wracked her body. "You big idiot...! Why did you heal me...? Why did you throw away pieces of your own life like that for someone like me?! Tell me honestly... was it worth it? Was saving someone as ruined and broken as me really worth shortening your lifespan?! Answer me!"
I answered without even a moment’s hesitation, nodding firmly. "Yeah... it was worth it. Every single second. Seeing you whole again makes it all worth it."
The room fell into a heavy, emotional quiet for a long moment, the weight of my words hanging in the air.

I continued calmly, my voice steady despite the fatigue. "And don’t blame anyone here — not Tachibana, not Yuko, and definitely not your Master. This was my choice. My decision alone. No one forced me."

Akane took a deep, shaky breath and looked at the others with a heavy, commanding expression that left no room for argument. "Yuko, Hitomi, Tachibana... go outside for a while. I need to talk to him privately. Now. Don’t come back until I call for you."

The three of them hesitated visibly, reluctance and worry etched on their faces, but they eventually obeyed. They filed out quietly, closing the door behind them with a soft click that echoed like a finality.

The second they were gone, Akane moved like a deadly shadow. In a flash, she grabbed my collar with both hands and yanked me upright with surprising strength, staring directly into my eyes from mere inches away. Her face was half-covered by her black assassin mask, but her striking red eyes were overflowing with hot tears and burning with raw fury.

"Why...?" she demanded, her voice shaking violently, almost feral. "Tell me, Jack... Why?! Don’t you want to live?! Why are you throwing your life away like this over and over again?! Answer me, you stupid idiot!!"
Her grip tightened painfully on my collar, wrinkling the fabric as more tears slipped down her cheeks, soaking into her mask.
"Do you have any idea how I felt watching you lie there motionless for hours?! I thought... I thought you were really going to die this time! My heart stopped every time your breathing slowed."

"Every single time you use that cursed power, I feel like my soul is being ripped out piece by piece! Why do you keep doing this to me?! Why can’t you just be selfish for once in your life and think about yourself, about your own future?!"

She shook me slightly, her voice breaking further into raw anguish. "You promised me... You swore you wouldn’t use it recklessly anymore! And yet here you are, healing Hitomi without a second thought about the cost!"
"What about Haruna? What about Yuko? Did you even stop for one moment to think about how we would survive — how we would keep living — if something happened to you?!"
Akane’s forehead pressed hard against mine, her breath ragged and warm against my skin, carrying the scent of salt from her tears.

"You big fool... I hate you... I hate you so much for making me worry like this, for making me feel this helpless... If you die, I swear I’ll follow you right after. I won’t let you leave me alone in this world... Do you understand?! I’ll end it all the moment you do!"
Her hands trembled violently as she held my collar, clearly torn between wanting to slap me, scream at me, and pull me into the tightest embrace imaginable.

paragraphs: Kasumi’s eyes flashed with anger, her hands clenching into fists. "Fumiko, that’s enough!" she hissed, her voice trembling with fury. "Jack is nothing like that! He’s kind, and respectful, and— and he cares about Haruna! If you say one more word against him, I swear—!"
Fumiko grinned triumphantly, leaning back with a satisfied sigh. "There it is." She pointed at Kasumi, her voice soft but firm.

"That’s how I know, Kasumi. You’re defending him. Fiercely." She paused, her gaze sharp. "A mother doesn’t get this angry unless she cares. And you, my dear friend... You care a lot. You love him, don’t you?"
Kasumi froze, her breath catching in her throat. "W-What are you talking about?!" she stammered, but her voice lacked conviction, her cheeks still flushed with anger and something deeper.
Fumiko smiled, her voice gentle but unyielding. "Kasumi, listen to me." She reached out, her hand pressing against Kasumi’s knee.

"I’ve known you for years. I’ve seen you happy, I’ve seen you sad, I’ve seen you angry... but I’ve never seen you like this." She paused, her eyes softening. "You’re flustered. You’re defensive. You’re blushing every time his name comes up. And you hate that I’m right."

Kasumi swallowed hard, her mind racing.[She’s... she’s not wrong...]But the shame was too much. "Fumiko... I don’t— I can’t—" Her voice broke, her eyes flickering toward the door, as if sensing my presence.

Fumiko leaned in closer, her lab coat shifting as she rested her elbows on her knees, her cleavage pressing together in a way that was both professional and distractingly alluring. "So you really do love him?" she asked again, her voice soft but insistent.

"See, you can’t even defend yourself." Her fingers tapped lightly against her chin, her eyes sharp and knowing. "You’re trembling, Kasumi. You’re blushing. You’re avoiding his name like it burns your lips."

Kasumi’s tears spilled over, dripping down her cheeks as she shook her head violently. "No... I can’t love him... He is my daughter’s... fiancé..." Her voice was a broken whisper, her hands clutching at her kimono so tightly her knuckles turned white.
"How am I supposed to...?" The pain in her voice was raw, unfiltered, as if the words themselves were tearing her apart.
I used my telepathy to tune into Fumiko’s thoughts, and what I heard painted a clearer picture of her intentions.

[I knew it... The way her eyes keep darting to him, the way her body tenses whenever he’s near... She’s fighting it, but it’s written all over her. But how can I help her as a psychologist? If this were a normal case, I could just tell her to cut off contact with Jack and let him and Haruna be together. But Kasumi’s different...]

[She’s been through so much. Loneliness, heartbreak... And now, for the first time in years, she’s alive again. And it’s because of Jack. Not her daughters—though she loves them—it’s him. She just doesn’t realize it yet...]
[Maybe I need to distract her. Make her see this isn’t love... not yet. It’s just care. It’s just gratitude. She’s confusing the two...]

Fumiko took a deep breath, her expression softening as she reached out, her hand gently lifting Kasumi’s chin so their eyes met. "Kasumi, here... look at me..." Her voice was warm, soothing, like a balm over an open wound.
"Don’t cry... You did nothing wrong... Why are you crying? Is there something wrong with loving someone?"
Kasumi shook her head, her tears still falling. "But he is my son-in-law..." Her voice was thick with despair, as if the words themselves were a sin she couldn’t forgive herself for.
Fumiko sighed, her fingers brushing away a tear from Kasumi’s cheek. "Kasumi..." she began, her voice gentle but firm.
"I think... you’re confusing care with love." She paused, her eyes searching Kasumi’s face.

"You’ve been alone for so long... and then Jack came into your life. He cares for you, doesn’t he? He spoils you, looks after you..." Her hand moved to Kasumi’s shoulder, squeezing lightly. "And you... You’ve taken that care and mistaken it for love."
Kasumi looked down, her fingers twisting the fabric of her kimono. "But... it feels like love..." she whispered, her voice barely audible.

Fumiko smiled softly, her thumb tracing circles on Kasumi’s shoulder. "Of course it feels like love, Kasumi. When someone treats you with kindness after so long... It’s easy to mistake it for something deeper."
She leaned in, her voice dropping to a whisper. "But ask yourself this... If Jack weren’t Haruna’s fiancé... if he were just a man you met by chance... would you still feel this way?"
Kasumi froze, her breath hitching. The question hung in the air, heavy and unanswered.
Fumiko continued, her tone gentle but persistent. "Or is it just that... for the first time in years, someone is looking at you? Seeing you? Not as a mother, not as a widow... but as a woman?"
She paused, her eyes softening. "That’s a powerful thing, Kasumi. It can feel like love... when really, it’s just loneliness finally being filled."
Kasumi bit her lip, her mind racing.[Is she right? Am I just... lonely?]The thought stung, but it also felt like a weight lifted. "But... what if it is love?" she whispered, her voice trembling.

Fumiko chuckled softly, shaking her head. "Oh, Kasumi..." She squeezed Kasumi’s shoulder. "If it is love... then you’ll know. And you’ll have to decide what to do about it." She paused, her gaze turning serious. "But for now... just breathe. You don’t have to figure it all out today."
Kasumi nodded, her tears slowing, her breath steadying. The confusion was still there, but the panic had eased. "Thank you, Fumiko..." she murmured, her voice small but sincere.
Fumiko smiled, standing up and adjusting her lab coat. "Anytime, Kasumi. That’s what friends are for." She paused, her eyes flickering toward the door—right where I was standing.
"And Kasumi..." Her voice turned playful. "If you do decide it’s love... well... just be careful. Men like Jack... they have a way of complicating things."
Kasumi blushed, her eyes darting to the door as well, as if she knew I was there. "Fumiko..." she warned, but there was no real anger in her voice.
Fumiko laughed, the sound rich and warm. "Alright, alright. Let’s finish your check-up before Jack starts wondering where we’ve disappeared to."

paragraphs: Kasumi shook her head, her voice firm. "No, this can’t be true... You don’t know anything about Jack... He is nothing like that..."

Standing invisibly there, listening to the confrontation, I was surprised that Fumiko could analyze things so clearly—that I was lusting after Kasumi’s body. But she was wrong about one thing: I would never hurt Kasumi... or any of my women.
I heard Kasumi’s thought, her voice bitter and resigned.[Hmm... What do you know...? I should have never come here...]
Fumiko noticed Kasumi’s angry look, her voice softening. "Kasumi... I am not advising you as a doctor, but more as a friend..." She paused, her gaze serious.

"If not for yourself, just think about your daughters... If I am right... If Jack is really lusting after your body... once he gets what he wants, he will leave you and your daughters after that..." She leaned in, her voice urgent. "Hurting your whole family... Can you really let that happen?"
Kasumi shook her head, her voice trembling. "Then what if you are wrong? What if Jack is not like that...?" She paused, her eyes pleading.
"Even if I don’t trust my judgment in recognizing people... I trust my Yuko’s judgment... my Haruna’s judgment... and even Tomiko..." Her voice grew stronger. "Are they all wrong?"

Fumiko sighed, her voice turning cold. "Kasumi, you don’t know these rich people..." She leaned back, her eyes dark. "They see us not as humans, but as their prey... and they want to hunt us..." She paused, her voice sharp.
"Why do you think Jack spends all his time... not managing his business empire, but spending his time with you and your family?" Her gaze was piercing. "He is clearly playing..."
Kasumi shook her head, her voice firm. "Fumiko... that’s enough..." Her eyes were cold, her tone final. "If you say anything against Jack... then we will not be friends..."
She paused, her voice trembling but defiant. "And whether Jack loves me or not... or if he is lusting after my body..." She looked up, her eyes burning with emotion.
"Then you are wrong... It is actually me who is lusting after him..." Her voice was raw, her confession shocking. "Are you happy now?"

"Kasumi... the things I said are just some ideas... I can also be wrong about it..." She paused, her gaze searching. "So how about we test whether Jack is just lusting after your body or loves you...?" Her voice turned sly. "What do you say?"
Kasumi shook her head, her voice firm. "No... Even if Jack doesn’t love me... I know he will never hurt my daughters or me..."
Fumiko leaned in, her voice teasing. "So you don’t want to know... he loves you...?" She paused, her eyes gleaming. "Or are you afraid your Jack... is just a lustful pervert?"
Kasumi shook her head, her voice defiant. "Jack is not like that..." She paused, her eyes burning with determination.
"I will prove it to you..." She leaned forward, her gaze sharp. "Tell me... how do you want to test Jack?" Her voice was steady. "I have complete trust in Jack..."

Fumiko smiled, her eyes gleaming with mischief. "I have an idea..." She paused, her voice turning serious. "I will forge your test results... which will show you need a kidney replacement... within 2 days..."

She leaned in, her voice dropping to a whisper. "Then we’ll see whether Jack is willing to help you... or if he will just run away, afraid you will ask him for help..." Her gaze was sharp. "What do you say? It will help you see his true face..."
Kasumi was silent, her mind racing.
Fumiko continued, her voice smooth. "I forget... Jack has quite a reach... Arranging a kidney in 2 days won’t be a big problem for him..."

She paused, her eyes gleaming. "I have a better idea..." Her voice turned darkly playful. "Let’s use heart failure as an excuse..." She leaned in, her voice a whisper. "Just see if Jack is willing to die for you..."

She paused, her gaze intense. "I will arrange a situation in which his heart condition will match yours... and if Jack gives his heart to you... He can save your life..." Her voice was sly. "What do you say?"
Kasumi gasped, her eyes wide. "NO... Fumiko, are you crazy...?" Her voice was horrified. "Are you trying to kill Jack...?"
Fumiko waved a dismissive hand, her voice calm. "We are not really hurting him... It’s just to see his reaction..."
Kasumi shook her head, her voice trembling. "Still... Fumiko... this is not right..." She paused, her eyes pleading. "Playing with him... If he knows... will he ever forgive me...?"
Fumiko leaned in, her voice gentle but firm. "Deep down... You also want to know the truth, right...?" She paused, her gaze sharp.

"Just listen to me... Even if I am wrong... then you can both laugh at me together..." She smiled, her voice turning playful. "And if I am right... It can save you and your family from a lot of pain... right...?"
Kasumi was lost, her mind spinning. "I... I..."

Fumiko grabbed Kasumi’s hand, her grip warm and reassuring. "Just leave it to me..." Her voice was firm. "Next, just pretend to be asleep here..." She paused, her eyes gleaming. "I will arrange everything..."
She picked up the landline, her voice sharp and professional. "Amanda... come here and bring a blood sample kit... to take a sample..."
Kasumi lay back on the recliner, her voice trembling. "What are you doing?"
Fumiko smiled, her eyes dark with mischief. "I am asking Amanda to collect a blood sample of Jack..." She paused, her voice turning sly.
"So that I can say to Jack that his blood sample and your sample are a perfect match... and a heart replacement can be done..." She leaned in, her voice a whisper.
"And give him 30 minutes..." Her gaze was sharp.
"I know for sure... There is no one in Japan... who can get a heart ready in 30 minutes..." She paused, her voice turning dark. "Leaving the choice up to Jack... to save you... or to let you die..."
Kasumi gasped, her eyes wide. "You are so cruel, Fumiko... We shouldn’t..."
Fumiko sighed, her voice soft but firm. "I am doing this for your good..." She paused, her gaze serious. "So that you won’t be deceived until the end..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1141 - 30 Minutes Deadline
paragraphs: I quickly teleported outside the examination room and removed my invisibility, just as the nurse could arrive any moment.

The sterile hospital corridor was eerily quiet, the fluorescent lights casting a cold glow over the polished floors. I leaned against the wall, my mind racing through the implications of Fumiko’s plan.
The weight of the situation pressed down on me. Fumiko was clever—brilliant, even—but she didn’t know me.
She didn’t understand that Kasumi was already mine, that her daughters were waiting for me to claim her. And she certainly didn’t realize that I would never let Kasumi die—not for a second.
After a few minutes, a nurse in a crisp white uniform approached me, her steps brisk and professional. "Are you Mr. Jack?" she asked, her voice polite but direct.

I nodded, extending my arm. She wasted no time, drawing my blood with practiced efficiency. The needle pricked my skin, the syringe filling with my deep red blood—A+, the same as Kasumi’s. Once the sample was taken, the nurse nodded curtly and left without another word.

I remained seated, my mind processing everything. About ten minutes later, I heard footsteps approaching—two nurses dragging a stretcher. They pushed through the door of Kasumi’s examination room and disappeared inside.
I knew the show was about to begin.

But one critical detail gnawed at me: a living person cannot donate their heart. It was medically impossible, legally forbidden. Fumiko knew this. Which meant her entire plan was a lie—a test designed to break Kasumi’s heart and force her to distance herself from me.

If I played along, Fumiko would convince Kasumi that I refused to save her life—that I didn’t love her enough to sacrifice myself for her. And just like that, Kasumi would believe I didn’t truly care, that my feelings for her were a lie.
Fumiko was trying to save Kasumi in her own way—protecting her from what she saw as a potential heartbreak, even if it meant breaking her heart now.
But she didn’t know the truth: Kasumi was already mine. And Yuko and Haruna knew it too. They were waiting for me to claim their mother as my own.
Fumiko hadn’t sensed this, but I had.
And I intended to turn her test against her.
Soon, the door to the examination room swung open, and Kasumi was wheeled out on a stretcher, her face pale, her eyes closed. But I knew better—she was pretending, just as Fumiko had planned.

I sprang into action, rushing to the stretcher, my voice laced with panic. "Oka-san! Oka-san...!" I grabbed her hand, my fingers intertwining with hers, and looked at Fumiko, my expression desperate. "Doctor, what happened to her? What’s going on?!"
Fumiko gave me a grave look, her voice professional but urgent. "Let’s get her to the ICU. We can’t say anything for sure yet..."

The nurses moved the stretcher toward the ICU, and I walked alongside, holding Kasumi’s hand tightly. "Oka-san, don’t worry... nothing will happen to you... You’ll be fine..." My voice was steady, but my heart raced with the thrill of the game.
Fumiko, Kasumi, and the nurses took her inside the ICU, and I was left to wait outside. The two nurses exited quickly, leaving me alone in the corridor.
I sat on a bench, pretending to be anxious and worried. But in reality, I extended my telekinesis and telepathy, sensing everything inside the ICU.

Inside the room, Kasumi opened her eyes, sitting up slightly as she looked at Fumiko. "Fumiko... let’s stop this..." Her voice was trembling, her eyes filled with guilt. "Didn’t you see Jack? He was hurt... His voice... he seems to be in so much pain..."
Fumiko sighed deeply, her thoughts a whirlwind of conflict.

[Kasumi has fallen head over heels for Jack... As her friend, maybe I should have just told her to go after him... But what kind of future would that be? She’d always feel guilty toward Haruna if they were together... And we don’t even know if Jack loves her for real... This way, at least her relationship with her daughter will remain intact...]
[Jack is not a fool... I can’t directly ask him to donate his heart... He knows it’s illegal to donate a heart from a living person unless they’re brain dead... So I can’t deceive Jack...]
[So I can only deceive Kasumi into thinking Jack is unwilling to donate his heart... Once that idea takes root, she’ll distance herself from him... This is the best outcome...]
I realized—Fumiko was exactly as I thought. But she didn’t know that I was the predator, and Kasumi was already mine.
Fumiko looked at Kasumi, her voice serious but gentle. "What? Have you already started thinking of him as your husband, Kasumi?"
Kasumi nodded, her voice firm but emotional. "Fumiko, I’m serious... I can’t bear to see him like this..."

Fumiko sighed, her heart heavy. "Okay... This will be over soon..." She paused, her gaze determined. "Now I will go out and tell Jack that you need a new heart... and I’ll accidentally reveal that his heart is compatible... Then we’ll see what his reaction is..."

She handed Kasumi her phone, the call already connected between them. "Here, take it... With this, you can hear his voice..." She pointed to the one-way mirror. "And you can see us through the observation window. Don’t worry—it’s a one-way mirror. You can see out, but no one can see in..."

Kasumi took the phone, standing up and moving closer to the observation window next to the ICU door. Through the glass, she saw me sitting on the bench, my head in my hands, my shoulders shaking as if I were weeping.
Fumiko walked out, carrying a document in her hand, her expression anxious. She approached me, handing me the file.
"Doctor, what happened to Oka-san? Is she okay?" I asked, my voice trembling with concern, my acting flawless.
Fumiko played her part perfectly, her voice grave. "She... her heart is showing signs of failure... We need to get her a new heart immediately..."
I nodded urgently, my voice firm despite the tremor. "Don’t worry, doctor... I will definitely find her a heart. Just give me a few hours..."
Fumiko shook her head, her acting impeccable. "Jack, we don’t have time... You have to hurry..."
She handed me Kasumi’s medical details—Blood Group: A+. "We need a heart with this blood type... and it has to be healthy..."
I asked anxiously, my voice breaking slightly. "How much time do we have?"
Fumiko didn’t hesitate. "30 minutes..."

"What?
Have you already started thinking of him as your husband, Kasumi?"
Kasumi nodded, her voice firm but emotional.
"Fumiko, I’m serious...
I can’t bear to see him like this..."
Fumiko sighed, her heart heavy.
"Okay...
This will be over soon..." She paused, her gaze determined.
"Now I will go out and tell Jack that you need a new heart... and I’ll accidentally reveal that his heart is compatible...
Then we’ll see what his reaction is..."
She handed Kasumi her phone, the call already connected between them.
"Here, take it...
With this, you can hear his voice..." She pointed to the one-way mirror.
"And you can see us through the observation window.
Don’t worry—it’s a one-way mirror.
You can see out, but no one can see in..."
Kasumi took the phone, standing up and moving closer to the observation window next to the ICU door.
Through the glass, she saw me sitting on the bench, my head in my hands, my shoulders shaking as if I were weeping.
Fumiko walked out, carrying a document in her hand, her expression anxious.
She approached me, handing me the file.
"Doctor, what happened to Oka-san?
Is she okay?" I asked, my voice trembling with concern, my acting flawless.
Fumiko played her part perfectly, her voice grave.
"She... her heart is showing signs of failure...
We need to get her a new heart immediately..."
I nodded urgently, my voice firm despite the tremor.
"Don’t worry, doctor...
I will definitely find her a heart.
Just give me a few hours..."
Fumiko shook her head, her acting impeccable.
"Jack, we don’t have time...
You have to hurry..."
She handed me Kasumi’s medical details—Blood Group: A+.
"We need a heart with this blood type... and it has to be healthy..."
I asked anxiously, my voice breaking slightly.
"How much time do we have?"
Fumiko didn’t hesitate.
"30 minutes..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1142: Kasumi’s Agony
paragraphs: Just then, Amanda walked in, handing Fumiko a report. Fumiko opened it, her eyes scanning the page before she looked up at me, her expression carefully neutral.
"Mr. Jack... take a look at this..." She handed me the report.
I saw it was my own medical file—Blood Group: A+.

Fumiko continued, her voice careful, testing. "Mr. Jack... would you like to donate your blood? I found your blood group also matches Ms. Kasumi’s..." She paused, her voice softening, as if gauging my reaction.
"I just wanted to create a medical profile for Ms. Suzuki’s family by asking Amanda to take your blood sample earlier... I didn’t expect it to match..."

I nodded, my voice breaking with raw emotion. "My blood sample and Oka-san’s are a match... then... then, Doctor..." I swallowed hard, my eyes filling with tears as I looked at her intently. "Can... can I donate my heart to Oka-san...?"

But I noticed Fumiko’s fingers twitch—she quickly muted the phone call, not letting Kasumi hear. Even though I knew Kasumi was watching us from behind the observation window, the ICU room was soundproof.
I sensed Kasumi’s thoughts, her mind racing with confusion and fear.
[What happened? I don’t hear anything... Why is Fumiko standing in front of Jack? Have they finished talking? What did he say...?]
Fumiko’s thoughts also echoed in my mind, panicked and shocked.
[OMG... Jack... what kind of man are you...? Thank God I muted the call in time... Otherwise, if Kasumi heard this, everything would be ruined...]
[Does he really love her? He’s willing to give his heart without even thinking...]
Fumiko adjusted her expression, her voice steady but firm. "Mr. Jack, you should know that this is impossible... and it is also illegal... for a living person to donate their heart..."
She paused, her gaze softening, but her voice remained resolute. "Mr. Jack... I think you should focus on finding a heart..."

I let the tears fall freely, wiping them away with the back of my hand as I nodded. "I will... I won’t let anything happen to her..." My voice was thick with emotion, my acting so convincing that even I almost believed it.
Fumiko nodded, then turned to walk back inside the ICU.
I nodded again, pretending to pull out my phone and making a call, my voice urgent as I barked orders into the receiver, demanding a heart be found within the hour.
As Fumiko re-entered the ICU, I sensed everything through my telepathy and telekinesis.
Kasumi asked urgently, her voice trembling, "Fumiko... what happened? I didn’t hear anything on the phone..."
Fumiko made an excuse, her voice smooth. "The signal must be weak inside the ICU..."
Kasumi asked again, her tears welling up as she watched me through the window, my shoulders shaking with feigned despair. "Why is he crying? What did he tell you...?"
Fumiko sighed, her voice heavy with false resignation. "He is trying to find a heart for you..."
But doubt crept into Fumiko’s mind, her thoughts conflicted and guilty.

[No... I can’t let Jack and Kasumi see each other... Otherwise, what if Jack talks to her? Then everything will be over... This is making me feel like an evil person... Maybe I should just... let them be together...]
[Hurting Jack like this... and Kasumi... Am I doing the right thing as a psychologist? Why do I feel like a villain, destroying people’s happiness?]
[ And seeing Jack... the way he’s protecting Kasumi... whether he loves her as a woman or thinks of her as a mother... it’s real... His eyes never lie...]
Kasumi couldn’t take it anymore.

She turned away from the window, her hands clutching her kimono as she paced the ICU, her breath coming in short, panicked gasps. "Fumiko..." she whispered urgently, her voice breaking. "Fumiko, please... I can’t... I can’t do this..."
Fumiko looked up, her eyes wide as she saw Kasumi’s distress. "Kasumi...?"

Kasumi shook her head, her tears streaming down her face. "He’s... he’s in pain..." Her voice was a sob. "I can’t... I can’t let him think I’m... I’m dying..." She clutched her chest, as if the thought was physically hurting her. "I can’t let him believe... that I’m leaving him..."
Fumiko sighed, her heart softening as she saw Kasumi’s agony. "Kasumi..." she whispered, her voice gentle. "This is the only way to know for sure..."
Kasumi shook her head violently, her voice rising. "No... No, it’s not..." She turned back to the window, her eyes locking onto me as I sat there, broken.
"Look at him, Fumiko..." Her voice was a plea. "He’s destroyed... He thinks he’s losing me..." She paused, her breath hitching. "And I... I can’t... I can’t let him believe that..."

She pressed her forehead against the glass, her voice a whisper. "I love him, Fumiko..." Her confession was raw, her heart laid bare. "I love him... and I can’t... I can’t let him think... that I don’t love him back..."
Fumiko was silent, her mind racing.[She’s... she’s in love with him... Truly, deeply...]

Kasumi turned away from the window, her voice trembling but firm. "Fumiko... I’m ending this..." She wiped her tears, her chin lifting with determination. "I’m going to him... I’m going to tell him..."
Fumiko reached out, her voice urgent, her fingers brushing against Kasumi’s sleeve. "Kasumi, wait—!"
But Kasumi was already moving, her kimono rustling softly as she stepped out of the ICU, her eyes locked on my back.
She didn’t yell, didn’t call out. Instead, her voice was choked, broken, as if the words were too heavy to speak aloud.
"J-Jack..." Her whisper was barely audible, her tears streaming down her cheeks as she watched me walking away, my shoulders still shaking with silent sobs.

I could feel her presence behind me, her emotions crashing like a storm—guilt, love, desperation. She wanted to call out, wanted to run to me, wanted to wrap her arms around me and never let go. But something held her back—fear, shame, the weight of her own feelings.

Fumiko followed Kasumi, her expression conflicted, her mind racing.[She’s going to him... She can’t bear to see him in pain...]But she didn’t stop her. She knew—this was bigger than her test, bigger than her fears as a friend.

Kasumi took a step forward, her hand trembling as she reached out toward me, as if she wanted to touch my shoulder, to pull me into her arms. Her breath hitched, her voice a whisper. "Jack..." The word was a prayer, a plea, a confession all in one.

chapters.title: Chapter 1143: The Last Call
paragraphs: I didn’t look back, didn’t let them know I knew they were there. Instead, I walked out of the main door, my shoulders trembling as if the weight of the world had settled on them. The cool hospital air hit my face, but I didn’t stop. I sat down on a bench outside, my mind racing with the next move.
I sensed Kasumi and Fumiko following me, their footsteps hesitant, their breaths shaky. Kasumi was about to reach me, her heart pounding in her chest, her mind a whirlwind of confusion and fear.
I pulled out my phone, my fingers trembling as I video-called Haruna.
"Hello, Jack..." Haruna’s cheerful voice filled the air as she picked up. I angled the phone carefully so she could only see me, not Kasumi and Fumiko standing behind me, frozen in shock.
Kasumi and Fumiko stopped in their tracks, their ears straining to catch every word.
"How are things at the hospital?" Haruna asked, her voice warm and concerned.
I smiled softly, my voice steady despite the turmoil inside me. "Nothing, Oka-san is fine... I just wanted to know how you’re doing..."

Haruna grinned, panning the phone to show Yuko and Tomiko sitting together in Tomiko’s office, chatting and laughing. "We’re having fun with Oba-san... in the company... We’re going to have lunch soon..."
Yuko leaned in, her eyes sparkling with curiosity. "Jack, how is Oka-san? Did the doctor say anything?"
I shook my head, my smile gentle but forced. "No... Everything is fine here. The doctor said Oka-san is in good health... Just asked her to rest for a few days..."
Yuko and Tomiko sighed in relief, their shoulders relaxing. "That’s good..." Tomiko said, her voice soft but laced with concern.
Tomiko leaned closer, her eyes narrowing as she studied my face through the screen. "Jack... what happened? You look down..." Her voice was laced with worry, her instincts as a sister sharp.
I shook my head, my voice quiet, my gaze avoiding the camera. "No... It’s nothing, Oba-san..."
I looked at the three of them—Haruna, Yuko, Tomiko—my heart swelling with love and determination. "I just wanted you to know..." My voice was firm, my gaze unwavering. "I love you..."
Haruna smiled brightly, her eyes shining with happiness. "I love you too..."
Yuko didn’t say it out loud, but she mouthed the words silently, her lips moving carefully while she kept an eye on Tomiko to ensure she wasn’t paying attention. "I love you too..."
I hung up the phone, my heart pounding as I sensed Kasumi’s thoughts behind me.
[What happened...? What is he saying...? Why does it sound like he’s saying goodbye...?]
[My heart... why does it hurt so much...?]
Fumiko was also stunned, her mind reeling with confusion and a growing sense of dread.
I didn’t waste a second. I instantly started recording a video with my front camera, my face raw with emotion, my eyes filled with unshed tears.
"Hello, Oka-san..." My voice was soft, my gaze direct, as if I were speaking only to her.

"I just wanted to say... I’m sorry..." I paused, my breath shaky, my heart aching. "But I want you to know... It’s not your fault... Don’t ever blame yourself..." My voice broke, the weight of my words heavy. "And also tell Haruna and Yuko that I love them..."

I swallowed hard, my tears beginning to fall. "And I... I also love Oka-san..." My confession was raw, my voice trembling. "Not as a mother... but as a woman..." I shook my head, my mind racing. "I don’t know when it started... but I can’t help myself when I’m around Oka-san..."

My voice was a sob, my heart lay bare. "I’m sorry I can’t say this face-to-face to you... But I will always live with you, Oka-san... Never leaving you..." My voice was a vow, my love eternal. "Whenever you miss me... feel your heart... and you will find me..."

I cried hard as I spoke, my emotions overwhelming me. Then, I chuckled to myself, my mind racing with mischief and determination.[This is going to be a masterpiece... Maybe I should try acting more often...]With that, I stopped recording.
I sensed Kasumi and Fumiko behind me, both shocked to their core, their minds reeling.
Kasumi was crying silently, her thoughts a storm of love, disbelief, and despair.[He loves me... He really loves me...]
Fumiko was stunned, her eyes wide, her mind racing with shock and guilt.[What is he saying...? No... No... Is he crazy...?]

I stood up, my heart pounding as I walked toward a man sitting on the other side of the bench. I asked him for a pen, and when he handed it to me, I paid him all the money in my wallet. He was more than happy to oblige, his eyes widening at the generous sum.
I pulled out a clean white paper I had bought from Sudix Store and wrote quickly, my hand steady despite the storm inside me:
"After my death, please give my heart to Kasumi Suzuki. And keep my information confidential. Never let her know who her heart belongs to..."
I signed the paper, then placed it on the bench with my phone on top of it, the video I had just recorded playing on loop.
Then, without hesitation, I plunged the pen into my carotid artery.
Blood spurted out like a fountain, drenching my shirt, the bench, and the ground beneath me in a macabre display.
The man who had given me the pen screamed, his eyes wide with horror, stumbling back as if he had witnessed a murder.
Fumiko ran forward, her voice a desperate, broken yell. "No... No... Jack... WAIT...!" Her hands outstretched, her face pale with terror.
But it was too late.
I stopped all my healing abilities, letting myself bleed, and pretended to sway on my feet before collapsing onto the bench, my body going limp.

Kasumi yelled, her voice breaking with grief. "JACK...!" She rushed to me, falling to her knees beside me, her hands pressing against my wound, her tears soaking into my shirt. "Jack... what are you doing...? Why are you committing suicide...? Are you crazy...?!" Her voice was a sob, her heart shattering into a thousand pieces.
I pretended to be fading, my voice a weak whisper, my eyes fluttering as if I were losing consciousness. "Oka-san... I’m even hallucinating about Oka-san..."
Kasumi cried out, hugging me tightly, her body shaking with sobbing. "Jack... what are you doing...? Why...? Why would you do this...?!" Her voice was raw, her grief overwhelming.

chapters.title: Chapter 1144: The Slap That Broke Fumiko
paragraphs: Kasumi’s sobs grew louder, her body shaking as she hugged me tightly, her tears falling onto my face. "Jack... please..." Her voice was a plea, her heart torn apart.
"Why are you doing this to me? To us?!" Her fingers dug into my shirt, her grip desperate, as if she could will me back to life through sheer force.
"I need you... Yuko needs you... Haruna needs you... How can you leave us like this?!" Her voice broke, her body wracked with sobs.
"You idiot... You fool..." She pressed her forehead to mine, her tears mixing with the blood on my skin. "Don’t you dare leave me..."

Fumiko’s voice was a roar as she yelled toward the hospital entrance."SOMEBODY HELP! WE HAVE AN EMERGENCY!"She pressed her hands against my artery, her own tears falling onto my chest, but I let my body go limp, my breathing shallow. The blood pooled beneath me, a dark, spreading stain.
I was lifted onto a stretcher and rushed to the ICU. As the doctors and nurses swarmed around me, I used my telepathy to freeze them in place, their movements halting as if time itself had stopped.
Then, I activated my healing factor, sealing the wound instantly, restoring my body completely. The pain vanished, but the emotional agony remained, a weight I knew I’d carry forever.

Outside the ICU, Kasumi and Fumiko sat in stunned silence, their emotions a storm of grief, guilt, and shock. Fumiko clutched the bloodstained paper and my phone, her hands shaking so violently the paper trembled.

She read my words over and over, her voice a broken whisper. "It’s all my fault... I pushed him to this..." Her tears dripped onto the paper, smudging the ink. "I was the one who caused this..." Her voice was thick with guilt, her mind haunted by the consequences of her test.
She looked at Kasumi, who was crying uncontrollably, her face buried in her hands. "I pushed him to death..." Fumiko whispered, her voice thick with guilt. "I was the one who caused this..."

Kasumi lifted her head, her eyes red and swollen from crying, her voice a trembling whisper. "Why does he want to do this...? Didn’t you say... You wanted to ask for his heart... to see his reaction...? Why does he want to commit suicide...?" Her mind was spinning, her heart unable to comprehend the depth of my love.

Fumiko nodded, her tears falling freely. "Because... Because... a living person cannot donate their heart..." Her voice broke, her guilt crushing her. "So he..." She couldn’t finish the sentence, her sobs choking her words.

Kasumi felt as if the world had stopped. Her legs gave out, and she collapsed to the floor, her hands clutching her chest as if she could physically feel her heart breaking. "When...? Why didn’t I hear it...?" Her voice was a whisper, her mind reeling.

Fumiko wiped her tears, her voice trembling. "It’s because I didn’t want you to hear it..." She paused, her guilt overwhelming. "So I muted the phone before he could reply... so you didn’t hear it..." Her voice was a confession, her shame palpable. "I was afraid... I was afraid you would fall in love with him... that it would eventually destroy your family... and that you might even get hurt in this relationship with no hope of recovering..."

She handed Kasumi the paper, her hands shaking. "I told him that it was illegal to donate a living person’s heart... so... he..." Her voice trailed off, her tears falling as she gestured to the words I had written.

Kasumi took the paper, her hands trembling as she read the words aloud, her voice breaking with each syllable. "’After my death, please give my heart to Kasumi Suzuki... and keep my information confidential... Never let her know who her heart belongs to...’" Her voice cracked, her mind unable to process the depth of my sacrifice. She pressed the paper to her chest, her body shaking as if the words themselves were tearing her apart.

Then, as if a dam had broken, her grief turned to rage. With a sudden, violent motion, she slapped Fumiko across the face, her voice a broken scream. "You..." Her hand trembled as she pulled it back, her tears streaming down her face.
"You killed him!" Her voice was a sob, her guilt overwhelming. "You should have stopped him...!" She collapsed against the wall, her body wracked with sobs.
"I shouldn’t have trusted you..." Her voice was raw, her words laced with despair. "I killed Jack... I killed him..." She clutched her head, her nails digging into her scalp.
"How will I face Yuko and Haruna...? How will I live with this...?" Her voice broke, her body shaking as if the weight of the world had settled on her shoulders.

She clutched the paper to her chest, her voice a whisper, her heart pouring out. "Why are you so foolish, Jack...?" Her tears fell like rain, her love and grief intertwined. "You’re only thinking about yourself..." Her voice trembled, her anger and sorrow battling within her.

"What about me...? What about Yuko... Haruna...?" She looked up at the ceiling, her voice breaking. "How are we supposed to live if something happened to you...? How...?" Her body collapsed under the weight of her emotions, her sobs echoing through the empty hallway.
Fumiko knelt beside her, her own tears falling, her voice a whisper. "Kasumi... I’m so sorry..." She reached out a trembling hand, but Kasumi flinched away, her body curling in on itself.
"I didn’t know... I didn’t think..." Her guilt was a physical pain, her mind haunted by the consequences of her actions. "I thought I was protecting you..."
Kasumi shook her head, her voice a broken sob. "No... No, it’s my fault..." She clutched her chest, her heart aching as if it had been ripped from her body.

"I should have told him... I should have stopped him..." Her voice was a whisper, her grief overwhelming. She pressed her fists to her eyes, her body shaking. "I loved him too..." Her confession was a whisper, a secret she’d buried deep inside. "I loved him... and now he’s gone..."
Fumiko’s breath hitched, her eyes widening as the realization dawned on her. "Kasumi... "

But Kasumi didn’t answer. She just sat there, crying, holding the paper that proved my love, her heart shattered beyond repair. And as she sobbed, her voice a broken whisper, I knew—she would carry this pain for the rest of her life.
