chapters.title: Chapter 1145: Kasumi’s Confession
paragraphs: I chuckled to myself, the sound bitter even to my own ears.[The plan is done.]The words echoed in my mind, a cold satisfaction settling over me. The doctors and nurses moved like puppets on strings, their actions precise, their expressions a mix of relief and professional detachment.

I ordered the nearest doctor to apply a bandage to my neck, right where the wound should have been. He didn’t question it. None of them did. Their minds were still under the subtle influence of my telepathy, their movements mechanical, their thoughts muted.
The doctor pressed the sterile white bandage against my skin, the adhesive cool against the unbroken flesh beneath.
As soon as it was in place, I dismissed him with a wave of my hand. "Go out and tell Kasumi the surgery was successful. Tell her I was saved. And transfer me to the ward."

The doctor nodded, his face blank, and left the room with the nurses trailing behind him. A moment later, I heard his voice, steady and reassuring, carrying through the door. "The patient is out of danger. We are shifting him to the ward. You can visit him there."

Kasumi and Fumiko let out a collective, shuddering breath, their bodies sagging as if the weight of the world had been lifted from their shoulders. Kasumi’s hands flew to her mouth, her tears spilling over as she whispered, "Jack is safe... Jack is fine... Thank God..." Her voice was thick with relief, but beneath it, I could sense the lingering fear, the unspoken what if.
Fumiko’s tears fell silently, her hands trembling as she clutched them together.
The stretcher began to move, the wheels squeaking softly against the linoleum floor. I kept my eyes closed, my breathing shallow, my body limp.
The nurses pushed me forward, their voices low and professional. "He is still unconscious. He will wake up once the anesthesia wears off."

Kasumi’s footsteps were quick, her presence a warmth at my side. "Jack... Jack..." Her voice was a broken whisper, her fingers brushing against my hand, her touch trembling. I could feel the heat of her skin, the desperation in her grip. She didn’t let go.

Fumiko followed, her footsteps heavier, her breath uneven. The stretcher rolled into the presidential suite of the hospital—a private, luxurious space reserved for the most critical or high-profile patients. The nurses transferred me to the bed, their movements gentle, their voices hushed. As soon as they left, the door clicked shut, leaving Kasumi and Fumiko alone with me.
Kasumi’s grip on my hand tightened, her voice a choked whisper. "Jack... I’m sorry... I’m so sorry..." Her tears dripped onto the white sheets, her body shaking with silent sobs.

She leaned closer, her forehead pressing against my hand, her breath warm against my skin. "I should have known... I should have stopped you..." Her voice broke, her guilt a physical weight pressing down on her chest.
Then, as if suddenly remembering Fumiko’s presence, Kasumi’s head snapped up. Her eyes, red and swollen, locked onto Fumiko with a fury that made the air between them crackle.
"What are you doing here?" Her voice was a low, dangerous growl, her grip on my hand tightening as if she were afraid Fumiko would try to take me away.

"Get out." The words were sharp, final. "I don’t want to see you. Because of you... I almost lost him." Her voice trembled, her anger and grief twisting together into something raw and ugly. "You wanted to kill him..."

Fumiko flinched as if struck, her face pale, her tears falling freely. "No... Kasumi..." Her voice was a broken plea, her hands reaching out as if to bridge the gap between them, but Kasumi recoiled, her body curling protectively over mine.

"I didn’t expect him to... to commit suicide..." Fumiko’s voice cracked, her guilt suffocating her. "I thought... I thought he would just... refuse. Or laugh it off. Or anything but this..." She pressed her fists to her eyes, her shoulders shaking. "I didn’t know he loved you this much..."

Kasumi’s breath hitched, her gaze flickering back to me, her thumb tracing the bandage on my neck. The sight of it—the physical proof of what I’d done—made her stomach twist. She turned back to Fumiko, her voice a venomous whisper.

"You used him. You tested him. And look what happened." Her free hand clenched into a fist, her nails digging into her palm hard enough to draw blood. "He almost died because of you. Because of your stupid test."

Fumiko’s knees buckled, and she sank to the floor, her back against the wall. She didn’t try to defend herself. There was nothing to say. The truth was a knife twisting in her gut. "I know..." Her voice was barely audible, her tears soaking into the fabric of her sleeves.

"I know..." She looked up at Kasumi, her eyes pleading. "But I didn’t mean for this to happen. I just... I wanted to see if he would fight for you. If he would choose you." Her voice broke. "I didn’t think he would sacrifice himself."
Kasumi let out a bitter, broken laugh, the sound hollow. "And what if he had died, Fumiko?" Her voice was a blade, sharp and unyielding.
"What then?" She gestured wildly at me, her other hand still clinging to mine. "Would you have been happy? Would you have been able to live with yourself, knowing you pushed him to this?"

Fumiko’s breath came in ragged gasps, her chest heaving. "No..." She shook her head violently, her hair whipping around her face. "No, I wouldn’t. I couldn’t..." She pressed her forehead to her knees, her voice muffled. "I was wrong... I was so wrong..."

Kasumi’s anger wavered for a moment, her grip on my hand loosening slightly. She looked down at me, her thumb brushing against my knuckles, her voice softening to a whisper. "Jack..." Her tears fell onto my hand, her love and guilt intertwining into something unbearable.

"You idiot..." She let out a shaky breath, her voice breaking. "You fool... Why did you do this? Why did you scare me like this?" Her free hand reached up, her fingers hovering over the bandage on my neck, as if she were afraid to touch it, afraid it would all disappear. "I can’t... I can’t lose you..." Her voice was a sob, her body shaking. "Not like this... Not ever..."

Fumiko watched them, her heart shattering. She had never seen Kasumi like this—so vulnerable, so broken. The realization that her actions had caused this pain was a weight she knew she would carry forever.
She stood slowly, her legs unsteady, her voice a whisper. "Kasumi... I’m sorry..." She took a step forward, her hand outstretched, but Kasumi flinched away, her body tensing.
"Don’t touch me," Kasumi hissed, her voice raw. "Don’t ever touch me again."

chapters.title: Chapter 1146: Desperate Kiss in the Hospital Bed
paragraphs: Fumiko’s hand fell to her side, her tears falling faster. "I’ll leave..." She turned toward the door, her steps heavy, her shoulders slumped. "But Kasumi..." She paused, her voice trembling. "Please... forgive me... someday..."

Kasumi didn’t answer. She couldn’t. Her gaze was fixed on me, her fingers tracing the lines of my palm, her voice a broken whisper. "Jack... please wake up..." Her forehead pressed against my hand, her tears soaking into the sheets.

"Please... I need to see you. I need to yell at you. I need to hug you..." Kasumi’s voice cracked, her body wracked with sobs, her fingers trembling as they clung to my hand. The warmth of her skin seeped into mine, her tears dripping onto the white hospital sheets, turning them translucent in spots. "I need to tell you... that I love you too..."
Her confession hung in the air, a fragile, trembling thing. And in that moment, I couldn’t bear it any longer.

I made the subtlest movement—a twitch of my fingers against hers. Kasumi froze, her breath catching in her throat as if she’d been struck. Her grip tightened, her eyes widening as she stared at my hand, her mind racing.
[Did I imagine that?]Then, slowly, as if afraid to break the spell, she lifted her gaze to my face.
I opened my eyes.

The first thing I saw was Kasumi—her face streaked with tears, her eyes red and swollen, her lips parted in shock. The relief in her expression was so overwhelming that it was almost painful to witness. "Jack...?" My name on her lips was a prayer, a plea, a whisper of disbelief.
I blinked slowly, my voice hoarse, as if I were still half-asleep. "Oka-san... you?"
Kasumi’s breath hitched, her hands flying to her mouth as if to stifle a sob. "Jack..." Her voice was a broken whisper, her tears falling faster.
"I—I’m sorry... I’m fine..." She shook her head violently, her words tumbling out in a rush. "There’s no problem with my heart. It was all Fumiko’s idea... to test you..."

I let my expression shift—first to shock, my eyes widening, my mouth falling open as if the words had physically struck me. Then, just as suddenly, I forced myself to calm, my features softening into something like relief.

My voice was rough, but steady. "What?" The word was sharp, laced with disbelief. Then, as if a weight had been lifted, I exhaled, my shoulders sagging. "It’s good... It’s good... It’s not true." I swallowed hard, my gaze locked on hers. "I’m glad you’re healthy, Oka-san... I..."
My voice trailed off, but the words hung between us, heavy with unspoken meaning—love, fear, regret, and something deeper, something that felt like fate.

Kasumi’s tears continued to fall, her hands trembling as she reached out, her fingers brushing against my cheek as if she needed to confirm I was real, that I wasn’t a ghost or a figment of her shattered imagination.

"Jack... you idiot..." Her voice was a mix of laughter and sobs, her relief so overwhelming it bordered on hysteria. She let out a broken chuckle, her breath hitching as she pressed her forehead to mine, her skin warm against my own.
"You scared me..." Her voice cracked, her fingers tightening against my face. "I thought I’d lost you..."

I looked at her, my gaze steady, my voice soft but firm. "Oka-san... I love you." The words spilled out of me, raw and unfiltered, the truth I’d carried for so long finally set free. "I regret not saying it to you before... when I heard you were dying."

My throat tightened, the memory of that moment still fresh, still painful. "I just... I don’t want to live with that regret." My voice was a whisper, my eyes never leaving hers. "I want Oka-san to know... that I love her. As a woman."

Kasumi’s breath hitched, a blush spreading across her tear-streaked face. She let out a shaky laugh, her voice barely above a whisper. "Still calling me Oka-san..." Her fingers traced the line of my jaw, her touch gentle, almost reverent. "I love you too, Jack..."
But then her expression hardened, her grip on my face tightening as if she were afraid I’d disappear if she let go. "But you..." Her voice trembled, her eyes burning with a mix of love and anger.

"How could you be so selfish?" Her voice broke, her tears falling faster. "Even if you wanted to save me... You shouldn’t have done that." She pulled back slightly, her hands still framing my face, her gaze searching mine.
"If something really happened to you... because of me..." Her voice was a whisper, her pain palpable. "Do you think I would have the will to live?" Her fingers dug into my skin, her desperation raw.
"How would I face Haruna and Yuko then?" Her voice cracked, her grief and fear intertwining. "So promise me..." Her voice was a plea, her eyes pleading. "Promise me you’ll never do that again..."

I pretended to hesitate, my gaze flickering away for a moment before I shook my head, my voice soft but unyielding. "I’m sorry, Oka-san..." I reached up, my hand covering hers, my thumb brushing away a fresh tear. "But I can’t promise you that." My voice was steady, my resolve unshaken.
"I can’t live knowing I could have saved you... But I didn’t." My eyes locked onto hers, my love and determination unwavering.

"So if there’s another chance... I would not hesitate to repeat it again." My voice was firm, my words a vow. "And this is not a mistake..." I shook my head, my gaze never wavering. "This is my choice."
Kasumi’s breath caught in her throat, her eyes widening as if she’d been struck. For a moment, she just stared at me, her chest heaving, her emotions a storm of love, fear, and frustration.

Then, without warning, she threw herself onto me, her body pressing against mine, her arms wrapping around me as if she could merge us into one. "You are a big idiot... big idiot..." Her voice was muffled against my chest, her tears soaking into my hospital gown.
And then, before I could react, she kissed me.

It wasn’t soft or gentle. It was desperate, hungry, a collision of lips and tears and years of unspoken love. Her hands gripped my face, her fingers tangling in my hair, her breath mingling with mine as if she were trying to breathe life into me.
The kiss was raw, real, and so full of emotion it felt like my heart might burst.
When she finally pulled back, her forehead rested against mine, her breath coming in ragged gasps. "Jack..." Her voice was a whisper, her eyes closed, her tears mixing with mine.
"You can’t leave me..." Her voice broke, her grip on me tightening. "Not like this. Not ever..."

I let out a shaky breath, my hands finding their way to her waist, pulling her closer. My voice was a whisper, my lips brushing against hers. "I won’t... Oka-san..." My promise was a vow, my love for her a force stronger than death itself. "I won’t..."

Her confession hung in the air, a fragile, trembling thing.
And in that moment, I couldn’t bear it any longer.
I made the subtlest movement—a twitch of my fingers against hers.
Kasumi froze, her breath catching in her throat as if she’d been struck.
Her grip tightened, her eyes widening as she stared at my hand, her mind racing.
[Did I imagine that?]Then, slowly, as if afraid to break the spell, she lifted her gaze to my face.
I opened my eyes.
The first thing I saw was Kasumi—her face streaked with tears, her eyes red and swollen, her lips parted in shock.
The relief in her expression was so overwhelming that it was almost painful to witness.
"Jack...?" My name on her lips was a prayer, a plea, a whisper of disbelief.
I blinked slowly, my voice hoarse, as if I were still half-asleep.
"Oka-san... you?"
Kasumi’s breath hitched, her hands flying to her mouth as if to stifle a sob.
"Jack..." Her voice was a broken whisper, her tears falling faster.
"I—I’m sorry...
I’m fine..." She shook her head violently, her words tumbling out in a rush.
"There’s no problem with my heart.
It was all Fumiko’s idea... to test you..."
I let my expression shift—first to shock, my eyes widening, my mouth falling open as if the words had physically struck me.
Then, just as suddenly, I forced myself to calm, my features softening into something like relief.
My voice was rough, but steady.
"What?" The word was sharp, laced with disbelief.
Then, as if a weight had been lifted, I exhaled, my shoulders sagging.
"It’s good...
It’s good...
It’s not true." I swallowed hard, my gaze locked on hers.
"I’m glad you’re healthy, Oka-san...
My voice trailed off, but the words hung between us, heavy with unspoken meaning—love, fear, regret, and something deeper, something that felt like fate.

Kasumi’s tears continued to fall, her hands trembling as she reached out, her fingers brushing against my cheek as if she needed to confirm I was real, that I wasn’t a ghost or a figment of her shattered imagination.
"Jack... you idiot..." Her voice was a mix of laughter and sobs, her relief so overwhelming it bordered on hysteria.
She let out a broken chuckle, her breath hitching as she pressed her forehead to mine, her skin warm against my own.
"You scared me..." Her voice cracked, her fingers tightening against my face.
"I thought I’d lost you..."
I looked at her, my gaze steady, my voice soft but firm.
"Oka-san...
I love you." The words spilled out of me, raw and unfiltered, the truth I’d carried for so long finally set free.
"I regret not saying it to you before... when I heard you were dying."
My throat tightened, the memory of that moment still fresh, still painful.
"I just...
I don’t want to live with that regret." My voice was a whisper, my eyes never leaving hers.
"I want Oka-san to know... that I love her.
As a woman."
Kasumi’s breath hitched, a blush spreading across her tear-streaked face.
She let out a shaky laugh, her voice barely above a whisper.
"Still calling me Oka-san..." Her fingers traced the line of my jaw, her touch gentle, almost reverent.
"I love you too, Jack..."
But then her expression hardened, her grip on my face tightening as if she were afraid I’d disappear if she let go.
"But you..." Her voice trembled, her eyes burning with a mix of love and anger.
"How could you be so selfish?" Her voice broke, her tears falling faster.
"Even if you wanted to save me...
You shouldn’t have done that." She pulled back slightly, her hands still framing my face, her gaze searching mine.
"If something really happened to you... because of me..." Her voice was a whisper, her pain palpable.
"Do you think I would have the will to live?" Her fingers dug into my skin, her desperation raw.
"How would I face Haruna and Yuko then?" Her voice cracked, her grief and fear intertwining.
"So promise me..." Her voice was a plea, her eyes pleading.
"Promise me you’ll never do that again..."
I pretended to hesitate, my gaze flickering away for a moment before I shook my head, my voice soft but unyielding.
"I’m sorry, Oka-san..." I reached up, my hand covering hers, my thumb brushing away a fresh tear.
"But I can’t promise you that." My voice was steady, my resolve unshaken.
"I can’t live knowing I could have saved you...
But I didn’t." My eyes locked onto hers, my love and determination unwavering.
"So if there’s another chance...
I would not hesitate to repeat it again." My voice was firm, my words a vow.
"And this is not a mistake..." I shook my head, my gaze never wavering.
"This is my choice."
Kasumi’s breath caught in her throat, her eyes widening as if she’d been struck.
For a moment, she just stared at me, her chest heaving, her emotions a storm of love, fear, and frustration.
Then, without warning, she threw herself onto me, her body pressing against mine, her arms wrapping around me as if she could merge us into one.
"You are a big idiot... big idiot..." Her voice was muffled against my chest, her tears soaking into my hospital gown.
And then, before I could react, she kissed me.
It wasn’t soft or gentle.
It was desperate, hungry, a collision of lips and tears and years of unspoken love.
Her hands gripped my face, her fingers tangling in my hair, her breath mingling with mine as if she were trying to breathe life into me.
The kiss was raw, real, and so full of emotion it felt like my heart might burst.
When she finally pulled back, her forehead rested against mine, her breath coming in ragged gasps.
"Jack..." Her voice was a whisper, her eyes closed, her tears mixing with mine.
"You can’t leave me..." Her voice broke, her grip on me tightening.
"Not like this.
Not ever..."
I let out a shaky breath, my hands finding their way to her waist, pulling her closer.
My voice was a whisper, my lips brushing against hers.
"I won’t...
Oka-san..." My promise was a vow, my love for her a force stronger than death itself.
"I won’t..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1147: Fumiko’s Path to Redemption
paragraphs: Kasumi instantly pulled back, her face flushing a deep crimson as if she’d just realized the weight of what she’d done. Her hands flew to her mouth, her eyes wide with a mix of shock and embarrassment.
"Y-You... wait..." Her voice was flustered, her gaze darting between me and the door. "I’ll bring the doctor... You’re still injured..."
Before I could protest, she bolted out of the room, her footsteps echoing down the hallway. A moment later, she returned with the doctor and nurses in tow.

I’d already used my telepathy to ensure they’d play their parts perfectly. They moved with practiced efficiency, checking my vitals, examining the bandage on my neck, and exchanging professional nods.

"He is showing good recovery," the doctor announced, his voice calm and reassuring. "There’s no problem. The wound wasn’t infected, and he could be discharged and taken home." He adjusted his glasses, his tone leaving no room for argument. "There’s no need to worry. Just don’t get water on your bandage."
Kasumi nodded, her shoulders sagging slightly in relief. "Thank you, doctor..."

As the doctors and nurses filed out, the door swung open again, revealing Fumiko standing in the doorway. Her face was pale, her eyes red-rimmed and swollen from crying. She hesitated for a moment, her gaze flickering between Kasumi and me, before stepping inside.
Kasumi’s body tensed, her voice sharp and unyielding. "What are youdoinghere?" Her hands clenched into fists at her sides, her anger a palpable force. "Get away."

Fumiko didn’t hesitate. She dropped to her knees in front of Kasumi and my bed, her head bowing low, her voice a broken whisper. "I’m sorry, Jack... Please forgive me..." She lifted her gaze, her eyes brimming with tears. "I’ve already resigned from my position. I know I’m not qualified to be a doctor..."
I noticed the way her coat gaped slightly as she knelt, the deep cleavage of her blouse revealing more than she likely intended. But there was no malice in it—only desperation, only regret.
Kasumi’s voice was a whip-crack. "Stop, Fumiko..."

I reached out, my hand finding Kasumi’s, my grip firm. My voice was soft but steady as I addressed Fumiko. "Ms. Fumiko... please don’t do this. I’m not angry..." I shook my head, my gaze sincere. "I want tothankyou."

Kasumi’s head snapped toward me, her eyes wide with disbelief. "Jack, what are yousaying?" Her voice was laced with frustration, her fingers tightening around mine. "Why do you want tothankher? For almostkillingyou?"

I shook my head again, my grip on Kasumi’s hand tightening as I lifted it slightly, as if to emphasize my point. "I want to thank Ms. Fumiko..." My voice was gentle, my eyes never leaving hers. "Maybe if this didn’t happen... I would never have been able to confess my feelings to Oka-san."
Kasumi’s breath hitched, her eyes glistening with fresh tears. The words hit her like a physical blow, her grip on my hand loosening slightly as she processed what I’d said.
Fumiko’s eyes widened, her surprise evident. She hadn’t expected forgiveness—let alone gratitude.

With Kasumi’s help, I shifted slightly, sitting up straighter in the bed. My voice was steady, my gaze flickering between the two women. "After hearing from Oka-san... I know this was just a misunderstanding." I paused, my voice softening. "I want Ms. Fumiko to continue to be Oka-san’s personal doctor."
Kasumi’s voice was a whisper, her confusion and emotion warring within her. "Jack, this..."

I turned to her, my free hand reaching up to brush a tear from her cheek. "Oka-san..." My voice was tender, my gaze unwavering. "Ms. Fumiko is your doctor. And she understands your situation best." I gestured slightly toward Fumiko, my voice firm.
"And she is also your friend. She can help you." My thumb traced circles against Kasumi’s skin, my voice gentle but persuasive.

"I know Oka-san is worried about her daughter... and now with me..." I let the words sink in, my gaze never leaving Kasumi’s. "You’ll at least have someone you can talk to... someone who can help you."

Kasumi’s breath trembled, her thoughts a whirlwind of conflict. I caught the flicker of her resolve through my telepathy:[That... yeah... Fumiko is my friend... She already knows my relationship with Jack... but she hurt Jack like that... Jack has already forgiven her... so...]
Kasumi’s voice was firm, her gaze shifting to Fumiko, though her grip on my hand remained tight. "Fumiko..." Her voice was a warning, her eyes sharp.

"I’m telling you... if youeverdo or say anything that hurts Jack..." Her voice dropped to a dangerous whisper, her free hand clenching into a fist. "Then I willreallyshow you no mercy." Her voice was cold, her threat unmistakable. "I will kill you myself if anything happens to Jack."

Fumiko’s breath hitched, her gaze dropping to the floor, her voice barely audible. "I understand..." Her shoulders shook slightly, her tears falling onto the polished hospital floor like scattered diamonds.

She didn’t look up again. With a final, shaky breath, she stood, her movements heavy with guilt, and left the room. The door clicked shut behind her, the sound echoing like a period at the end of a painful Chapter.
Kasumi’s phone rang instantly, the sudden chime cutting through the silence. She picked it up, her thumb hovering over the screen for a moment before she answered, putting it on speaker.

Haruna’s voice filled the room, bright and warm, completely unaware of the emotional storm we’d just endured. "Oka-san... are you still in the hospital? How long will it take to come back? We’re all at home... waiting for you guys."

Kasumi’s gaze flickered to me, a flicker of guilt passing over her face. I glanced at the clock on the wall—9 P.M. The night had slipped away from us, stolen by the chaos of emotions, near-tragedies, and confessions. I gave her a small, reassuring nod, my hand squeezing hers gently.
Kasumi cleared her throat, her voice steady despite the tremor in her hands. "We... we will be back soon... We just went out for shopping for a while..."
Haruna’s voice was cheerful, oblivious to the weight of the moment. "Ok... Ok... Don’t forget to buy me something... Bye..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1148: Japanese Lingerie store
paragraphs: Kasumi ended the call, setting the phone down on the bedside table. She turned to me, her eyes still glistening, but there was a softness there now, a quiet gratitude that made my chest tighten.
I reached for her hand, my thumb brushing over her knuckles, my voice gentle. "Don’t worry," I said, my voice firm but soothing.

"I’ll handle everything. I won’t let you or Haruna or Yuko down." My gaze locked onto hers, my promise absolute. "I’ll give you all the happiness in the world. I’ll never let you suffer any grievance."

Kasumi’s breath hitched, and before I could say another word, she leaned in, wrapping her arms around me in a tight embrace. Her cheek pressed against my shoulder, her voice muffled against the fabric of my hospital gown. "Thank you..." she whispered, her grip unyielding, her body trembling slightly. "Thank you for loving me..."
I held her just as tightly, my chin resting on the top of her head, my heart swelling with a love so fierce it ached.
For a moment, we just breathed, the weight of the day melting away in the warmth of her embrace. The scent of her hair—something floral, like cherry blossoms—filled my senses, grounding me.

After a while, Kasumi pulled back slightly, her hands still resting on my shoulders, her voice soft but laced with concern. "Can you move?" Her eyes searched mine, her fingers tracing the bandage on my neck. "If you want, we can stay tonight at the hospital..."
I shook my head, my voice light but firm. "I’m totally fine. Let’s go." I gave her a small smile, my fingers brushing a stray tear from her cheek. "Don’t let our daughter wait."

Kasumi froze, her eyes widening as the word registered. "Our... daughter...?" Then, as if the realization hit her all at once, a deep blush spread across her face, her cheeks turning a shade of pink that rivaled the setting sun.
She swatted my chest lightly, her voice a mix of exasperation and affection. "You’re so bad... They’re my daughters..."
I grinned, my voice teasing, my eyes sparkling with mischief. "Oh? Then..." I leaned in slightly, my breath warm against her ear, my voice dropping to a whisper. "Aren’t you my woman?"

Kasumi’s face turned an even deeper shade of red, her hands flying to her cheeks as if to hide her embarrassment. "Don’t talk..." she hissed, but there was no real anger in her voice, only a flustered warmth that made my heart race.
With that, we were discharged from the hospital, the cool night air a welcome change from the sterile scent of the ward.

The city lights twinkled like stars fallen to earth, casting a golden glow over the streets as Kasumi drove, her hands steady on the wheel. I watched her from the passenger seat, the faintest smile playing at the corners of her lips, her profile illuminated by the dashboard lights.

As we neared home, I turned to her, my voice casual but laced with amusement. "Oka-san... didn’t you tell Haruna we were shopping?" I raised an eyebrow, my tone innocent but my eyes glinting with mischief. "It’s not good to go back empty-handed..."
Kasumi’s smile widened, and she nodded, pulling the car into the parking lot of a high-end shopping center.

The building was a marvel of modern architecture, its glass facade reflecting the neon lights of the city. The air was alive with the hum of conversations, the scent of perfume, and freshly brewed coffee wafting from the cafes inside.
We walked through the shopping center, the polished marble floors reflecting our steps. Kasumi led the way with a newfound energy, her earlier exhaustion replaced by a quiet determination.

She picked out clothes for Haruna, Yuko, and Tomiko with care, her eyes lighting up as she imagined their reactions. I watched her, my heart full, as she held up a soft, pastel-colored sweater for Haruna, her fingers tracing the fabric with a mother’s love.

Then, with a mischievous glint in my eye, I tugged her toward a lingerie store on the upper level. The store was a sanctuary of elegance and sensuality, its entrance framed by delicate lace curtains that swayed gently in the air conditioning.
The lighting was soft and warm, casting a golden glow over the displays of silk, satin, and lace in every shade imaginable—deep blacks, soft pinks, fiery reds, and ivory whites.
Mannequins posed in the window, adorned in sets that ranged from demure to daring, their forms accentuating the curves the lingerie was designed to celebrate.

Kasumi’s steps faltered as we approached, her face flushing a deep crimson. She shot me a wide-eyed, horrified look, her voice a whisper. "J-Jack..." Her fingers tightened around mine, her gaze darting around as if afraid someone from her past might recognize her. "We can’t... I can’t..."

I ignored her protests, my grin widening as I pulled her inside. The scent of the store was intoxicating—a mix of lavender, vanilla, and something uniquely feminine. A soft, instrumental version of a pop song played in the background, the melody adding to the intimate atmosphere.
The walls were lined with plush velvet displays, each one showcasing a different collection.

To our left, a rack of bras in every size and style stretched toward the ceiling, their lace and embroidery catching the light. To our right, rows of panties—bikinis, thongs, boyshorts—were arranged like works of art.
A female attendant, a woman in her late twenties with a warm smile and an air of professionalism, approached us almost immediately.

She was dressed in the store’s uniform—a sleek black dress that complemented her figure, her dark hair pulled into an elegant bun. "Good evening," she greeted, her voice smooth and welcoming. "How may I assist you today?"
Kasumi’s face burned, her free hand flying to her mouth as if to stifle a gasp. "Ah—no, we’re just—"
I cut in before she could finish, my voice charming but casual. "We’re looking for something special." My gaze flicked to Kasumi, my eyes twinkling. "For her."
The attendant’s smile widened, her gaze shifting to Kasumi with a knowing look. "Of course. For a special occasion, perhaps?"
Kasumi let out a squeak, her face turning an even deeper shade of red. "N-No! It’s not like that—"
I chuckled, my arm slipping around Kasumi’s waist, pulling her closer. "It’s exactly like that."
The attendant laughed softly, her eyes sparkling with amusement. "I see. Well, you’ve come to the right place." She gestured to the displays around us.
"We have a wonderful selection of sets. Would you like something romantic? Seductive? Or perhaps something comfortable yet elegant?"
